messages:
Avery Johnson: Hey #help — quick Q from Sales/PM side. What’s the correct way to request Support help for a customer escalation (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)? Trying to avoid pinging random people. What info do you need up front?

Dev Patel: Thanks Avery. TL;DR: start with a SUP ticket unless it’s an active widespread outage.

Dev Patel: If you’re escalating on behalf of a customer:
1) Create/locate the Jira SUP ticket (preferred) and add “Customer Escalation” label.
2) Drop link here or in #support with the ticket + context (template below).
3) If it meets paging criteria (P0/P1), we’ll open a bridge and pull on-call.

Dev Patel: Template (copy/paste):
- Customer name + tier (self_serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)
- Product surface: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
- Region(s):
- Model + version (if pinned):
- Endpoint: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank/etc
- Time window (start time + “still ongoing?”):
- Impact (how many users/requests affected, severity in customer words):
- Errors (HTTP codes, error strings) + sample request IDs (2–5):
- Recent changes (SDK upgrade, config change, deploy, traffic spike):
- Mitigation attempted (retries, region failover, lowering max_tokens, etc)
- Customer comms status (have we acknowledged? next update due?):

Owen Phillips: +1. Biggest thing that slows us down is missing request IDs + region/model. If we have those, we can usually confirm in telemetry quickly.

Owen Phillips: Also: please don’t DM engineers directly for “can you take a look” — it bypasses our SLA timers + audit trail. Link a SUP and we’ll route.

Avery Johnson: Got it. When is it ok to “page” vs just file the SUP and wait?

Rafael Mendes: From SRE/on-call side: page only for customer-impacting incidents that are time-sensitive.

Rafael Mendes: Rough guidance:
- P0/page now: auth outage, 5xx spike, major region degradation, widespread timeouts, dedicated cluster down, private install/upgrade blocked with production down.
- P1/page during coverage: severe degradation w/ real business impact, no workaround, multiple customers, or enterprise SLA update cadence needed.

Rafael Mendes: If you’re unsure, still file SUP + post in #support with “possible P0/P1, need triage” and we’ll make the call.

Rachel Kim: From CS side: please include “customer expectations + next touchpoint.” If you have a promised update time, add it in the SUP so we can align.

Rachel Kim: Also note: don’t promise credits/penalties in email or calls. If customer is asking, flag in SUP and we’ll follow the exec escalation protocol.

Chris Osei: PM/Product Ops note: if it’s a product gap/bug (not an outage) still start as SUP. Support will link to Linear if it needs eng follow-up. Helps us keep severity language consistent.

Priya Shah: Self-serve/Hosted issues: before escalating, check Known Issues index + any workaround articles. If there’s a matching known issue, link it in the SUP and send the customer the workaround (Support can help with wording).

Priya Shah: (Internal) Known issues landing: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Known+Issues+and+Workarounds

Elliot Price: Docs side: if you find a recurring “how do I…” question that’s not in KB, drop it in #docs with the SUP link. We’re using that list for the known-issues sprint.

Avery Johnson: For Dedicated customers, what’s the minimum info? Sometimes they just say “latency is bad.”

Dev Patel: For Dedicated, ask for:
- Dedicated deployment name/ID (or org + environment)
- Region
- What changed recently (traffic, autoscaling config)
- Dashboard screenshots if they have them (or time range)
- Request IDs if they’re calling our API through a gateway

Dev Patel: If they can’t provide request IDs (some customers don’t log them), we can still work with timestamps + org + route.

Naomi Feldman: Security/compliance reminder: don’t paste customer logs containing PHI/PII into Slack. For sensitive logs, use the secure upload flow (Support can provide link) and reference the artifact in the SUP.

Owen Phillips: +1. If the customer wants to share packet captures / installer logs (Private), route them through the approved upload path and keep Slack summaries high-level.

Avery Johnson: Perfect. Is there a single place we can point folks to for this template + where to post?

Dev Patel: Yep — we just published the escalation playbook + intake checklist. Use these:
- Intake checklist (what to collect): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Support+Triage+Intake+Checklist
- Escalation paths + contacts: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Escalation+Paths+and+Contacts
- Severity matrix: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Severity+Matrix+and+Escalation+Triggers

Rachel Kim: If anyone on Sales needs a quick rule: “SUP first, then #support, then bridge if P0/P1.”

Rafael Mendes: And if there’s a suspected broad incident, move to #incidents once Support/SRE confirms. We try not to open #incidents threads for single-customer issues unless it’s truly systemic.

Avery Johnson: Super helpful. I’ll share this with the team. :thumbsup:

Dev Patel: Thanks. If you want, we can do a 15-min “how to escalate” walkthrough in the next Sales standup — low overhead.

Avery Johnson: Yes please — I’ll DM you scheduling.
